# Atomic Notes

> Atomic Notes is a free, local-first notes app for Android. Notes live on the phone first and sync to a private My-Atomic-Notes folder in the user's own Google Drive. An optional vault encrypts every note on the device with AES-256-GCM (key derived from a 6-word recovery phrase with Argon2id), so the sync server and Google store only ciphertext. The app has no AI features, no ads, and no analytics. Current version: 2.03.5, released 2026-09-28. Android 9 or newer. The source code is public to read and verify, but proprietary (Atomic Notes Source-Available License, all rights reserved). It is not open source. Built by Ashutosh Sharma (DevBehindYou).

Key facts:

- Storage: on-device first (Hive). Sync writes one .atomic file per note to the user's Google Drive, using the drive.file scope (the app sees only files it created).
- Server: stores metadata only (note IDs, pinned and deleted flags, timestamps, Drive file IDs). It never stores note titles or text. With the vault off, note text passes through it in transit to Drive.
- Price: free. Every account holds 30 notes. Cloud sync uses Atomic Energy: +20 every 24 hours, cap 120, standard sync 5 (at most once an hour), instant sync 10, syncs with nothing to upload are free. 1 Atomic Coin = 40 energy. New accounts get 5 coins. Coins are not sold in the app yet. Early supporters on Patreon (https://www.patreon.com/cw/DevBehindYou) or Ko-fi (https://ko-fi.com/devbehindyou) who send their account email get Atomic Coins from the developer by hand.
- Capacity tiers: Tachyon 30 notes (free), Antimatter 40 (10 coins), Monopole 50 (20 coins), Strangelet 100 (30 coins).
- Device security: biometric lock, TOTP two-step verification, blocked screenshots (FLAG_SECURE), Android secure storage.
- Distribution: signed APKs on GitHub Releases. Certificate SHA-256 cc24ae5ce1dca50fcd5e5c4c252d69e4965c55a975bd0e4739e8938fad9bebeb. Not on Google Play. No iOS build yet.

## Blog posts

- [What Is a Local First Notes App and Why Does It Matter?](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/what-is-a-local-first-notes-app): local-first software defined, offline first vs local first, the seven Ink & Switch ideals, how Atomic Notes syncs, and the tradeoffs
- [Notes App Privacy in 2026: 9 Red Flags to Check First](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/notes-app-privacy-red-flags): nine checks for any notes app (accounts, export, encryption keys, permissions, ads, trackers, AI, formats, storage) and how Atomic Notes scores
- [Encrypted Notes Explained: T2T vs End to End Encryption](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/encrypted-notes-explained): HTTPS vs at rest vs end-to-end, the Atomic Notes vault (Argon2id, AES-256-GCM), what encryption can't hide, and the recovery trade-off
- [Notes App Without Internet: Why Offline Should Be the Default](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/why-notes-should-work-offline): what works offline in cloud-first vs local-first apps, an airplane-mode test, and how sync catches up
- [Notes App Metadata: 8 Things It Knows Without Reading Notes](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/notes-app-data-collection): the metadata a notes app can collect, what it reveals, data minimization, and exactly what the Atomic Notes server keeps
- [Local First Architecture: 4 Layers Behind Atomic Notes](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/atomic-notes-architecture): the device, metadata-only sync server, user-owned Google Drive, and optional vault, with failure modes and the tech stack
- [7 Best Private Notes Apps for Android in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/best-privacy-first-notes-apps-android): Atomic Notes, SilentNotes, CypherLeaf, NoteSR, Quillpad, Fossify Notes, and Privacy Friendly Notes, checked October 7, 2026
- [6 Best Local First Note Taking Apps in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/best-local-first-note-taking-apps): Atomic Notes, Obsidian, Logseq, SiYuan, SilverBullet, and Trilium Notes, compared on primary copy, file format, sync, and encryption, checked October 9, 2026
- [5 Best End to End Encrypted Notes Apps in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/best-end-to-end-encrypted-notes-apps): Atomic Notes, Notesnook, Standard Notes, Cryptee, and Joplin, compared on key ownership, default encryption, recovery, audits, and metadata
- [8 Best Offline Notes Apps for Android in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/best-offline-notes-apps-android): Atomic Notes, Material Notes, Open Notes, sNotz, Easy Notes, Orgzly Revived, Notes, and Butterfly, checked for internet permission, account, sync, and backups
- [7 Best Note Taking Apps Without AI in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/best-note-taking-apps-without-ai): Atomic Notes, Markor, TiddlyWiki, Zim, Saber, Dynalist, and CherryTree, plus Notion alternatives without AI and how to check an app for AI
- [Notes App Security: 10 Privacy Mistakes to Fix in 2026](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/notes-app-privacy-mistakes): ten everyday habits that weaken notes app security (locks, secrets, share links, cloud accounts, exports, APKs) and a fix for each
- [Storing Passwords in Notes App: 5 Real Dangers](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/storing-passwords-in-notes-app): why a notes app is not a password manager, Google Keep and Samsung Notes for passwords, a breach check, and how to move passwords out
- [How Does Encryption Protect Privacy? 5 Gaps in Your Notes](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/encrypted-notes-privacy): transport encryption, key custody (iCloud Advanced Data Protection, Google Keep, Atomic Notes), metadata, analytics, and account recovery
- [Switch Notes App Safely: 7 Checks Before You Move](https://atomic-notes.devbehindyou.com/blog/switch-notes-app): export formats of popular notes apps, a migration plan with a rollback copy, and how to get notes out of Atomic Notes today
